subject: Random effects correlation estimates are always positive

messages.author: 077be7d21770b72d
messages.subject: Random effects correlation estimates are always positive
parts:
Hello,


I am fitting a model to data sets which have been simulated to display properties of a 2x2 design, each factor having two levels. There are two fully crossed groups, representing “subjects” and “items”. I constrain the groups' random intercepts and slopes to display certain patterns of correlation, which I give below. The known population parameters for correlation are denoted rho_subj and rho_item and the known sample correlations are denoted r_subj and r_item. The function two_by_two_gen.R which generated this data set is attached.


              intercept-factorA    intercept-factorB    factorA-factorB

rho_subj  0.6                       0.6                       0.6

r_subj      0.505                   0.629                    0.507

rho_item  0                         0                          0

r_item     0.147                   0.115                    -0.050


I let the eta parameter of the lkj correlation matrices vary among the values 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, and 4. For any given fit the lkj prior for the by-subject and the by-item correlation matrices have the same eta-parameter. The RStan code is given in the file two_by_two_sens_sim.R. Note that there are five models, and they differ only with respect to the shape parameter eta.


In general, the results are consistent with my expectations. More posterior density lies over the interval [0,1] than over the interval [-1,0]. This should obviously be the case for by-subject random effect correlations, since the known correlation parameters are positive. For by-item random effect correlations, however, the population correlation parameters are zero. For lower eta, we know that the estimates are going to be less conservative, and indeed they are. But it is worrisome to me that they always choose to go rightward, even for the correlation between slopes, whose sample correlation is somewhat negative. I had R write a PDF file with the plotted posterior pdfs for the by-item rhos.


I worry that this has to do with the direction of the fixed effects, which are both positive. But the fixed effects should be independent of the random effects, and of course also independent of the correlations between these. Has anyone experienced this before? Thanks for your help.



Tanner Sorensen
